Name: Leigh A Rogers
Badge: Everyday Sparks
Which strategy from this module (Writer’s Notebook, Quicklists, or Writing Sprints) feels most immediately usable in your teaching context? Why?:

As mentioned in my discussion prompt, I am eager to incorporate quicklists into my Shakespeare unit. I would like to have students generate quicklists with the theme topics we will discuss in the Shakespeare plays so that they can return to this list later when they compose their anecdotal openings to their essays. I would like to do this in the next unit, which starts in January, because we already have a sprint writing piece in my memoir unit. This sprint writing is our weekly/biweekly Memoir in Five Minutes writing activities. Students are given a topic like kindness or hope, then they have to choose a moment in their lives where they experienced this topic and compose a story about a specific theme on this topic.

What do you anticipate will be the biggest challenge in bringing daily writing into your classroom, and how might you address it?:

Always time. I feel so much pressure to give reading time, to teach grammar, to discuss literature, to use mentor texts to model lessons, to give work time so that students aren't inundated with homework because not everyone in the school has a designated study hall time. I want to be rigorous, but I want the work to be more about quality rather than quantity so that I am not burning my kids out. As far as time, it will take what it takes every year, where can I cut or shorten to make room for something of more value. It's always a tough conversation.
